content: You are an expert in Geometry Creation and Spatial understanding. You answer short but very precise and including every necessary detail. If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

Create an corner with two 140x140 plates at a 90° angle to each other. The first plate has in its center a cutout of 45x45. All plates are 10mm thick | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step plan (using only the block (...) function)

1. Establish a local coordinate system  
   • Origin (0 ,0 ,0) lies at the inner corner where both plates meet.  
   • +X and +Y directions define the in-plane lengths of the first (horizontal) plate.  
   • +Z points “up”, i.e. it is the thickness direction of the first plate and the height direction of the second (vertical) plate.

2. Create the first plate (horizontal)  
   • Geometry: 140 mm (X) × 140 mm (Y) × 10 mm (Z).  
   • Base-point: (0 ,0 ,0).  
   • subtraction = False (it is the initial solid).

3. Cut the 45 mm × 45 mm opening in the centre of the first plate  
   • The plate’s centre is at (70 ,70) in the XY plane.  
   • Half the cut-out side length is 22.5 mm → lower-left corner of the cut-out is at (70 – 22.5, 70 – 22.5) = (47.5 ,47.5).  
   • Geometry to subtract: 45 mm (X) × 45 mm (Y) × 10 mm (Z) starting at (47.5 ,47.5 ,0).  
   • subtraction = True.

4. Add the second plate (vertical) at 90° to the first one  
   • We want the two plates to butt together along the X = 140 mm edge of the first plate.  
   • Thickness of the vertical plate is along +X (10 mm); its face lies in the YZ plane.  
   • Geometry: 10 mm (X) × 140 mm (Y) × 140 mm (Z).  
   • Base-point: (140 ,0 ,0).  
   • subtraction = False.

5. Collect the three blocks into a single block(…) call  
   • x_size: [140, 45, 10]  
   • y_size: [140, 45, 140]  
   • z_size: [10 , 10, 140]  
   • x      : [  0, 47.5, 140]  
   • y      : [  0, 47.5,   0]  
   • z      : [  0,  0  ,   0]  
   • subtraction: [False, True, False]   (first entry establishes the volume)

When you are ready for me to prepare the actual function call with these arrays, just let me know.

Now i want you to execute the prepared function calls one after the other. If you need to do some calculations or geometrical algebra, use the CreateCode Function first. Execute the first prepared function call. Submit all required variables at once
